newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nearby soybeans end higher on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nearby soybeans end higher on fund buying.

text.p: Nearby CBOT soybean futures ended higher on Thursday as funds bought at least 20 million bushels but new crop months closed lower on hedge sales tied to increased farmer selling, traders said.
Griffin Trading reportedly bought 10 million bushels of soybeans in the last hour of trade. Cargill Investor Services bought seven million bushels on the day, traders said.

USDA's weekly export data also lent support. USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soybeans for the week ended February 7 totaled 582,700 tonnes, above expectations for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
Bears pointed out there were heavy cancellations and export shipments were down from the week before. USDA reported reductions of 237,400 tonnes for unknown destinations.

Bullish plays in the options pit also supported soybeans. Continental Grain reportedly bought 850 July $7.75 calls at 29-3/4 cents and sold 850 July $8.75 calls at 10 cents. The commercial firm also sold 400 July $7.50 puts at 27-1/2 to 28 cents, traders said.
Soybeans closed three cents per bushel higher to 2-3/4 cents lower with March up 1-1/4 at $7.65-1/2. New crop November closed 2-3/4 cents lower at $6.98-3/4.
Increased farmer selling contributed to the losses in new crop soybeans, traders said. Cash sources said Wednesday's rally prompted active sales of old and new crop soybeans.

They said farmers had been waiting for a move above $7.50 in the March and $7.00 in the November. March closed Wednesday at $7.64-1/4, a four-month high, while November ended at $7.01-1/2, the first close above $7.00 since October 10.

On the day, Prudential Securities bought 3.5 million bushels May and 2.5 million March, traders said, while Refco Inc bought two million May and Iowa Grain and LIT America each bought two million March.
Technical traders noted the March and May contracts closed above the four- and 20-day moving averages for the second day. Short-term technical signals were bullish, they said.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 70,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 85,103 contracts.
